Alex — great speaking this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary:
- Primary use: customer support augmentation (answer retrieval + structured tool calling for intents) and transaction enrichment (embeddings + reranker for candidate retrieval).
- Traffic estimate: 10k requests/day initially, peak bursts to 1.5x around payroll windows.
- SLO: 95th pct latency requirement ~300ms for user-facing paths; async/nearline okay for heavy rerank jobs.

Integration notes (high-level):
- SDKs: we have first-class SDKs for Python/Node/Go. Init & request flow is simple (snippet below) and supports explicit routing and model pinning.
- Auth: API key by default; Dedicated/Private supports KMS-backed keys and OIDC for enterprise SSO. Key rotation and short-lived creds supported.
- Routing: policy-level routing (latency vs cost vs model version) + per-request hints.
- Structured output / tool calling: Redwood can return structured JSON with schema validation or call external tools (tool-calling) with guarded outputs.
- Embeddings + reranker pattern: embeddings for candidate retrieval, then reranker as a cross-encoder or lightweight ranker for precision.
- Observability hooks (requested): we expose trace headers and latency breakdown headers you can propagate into your system to correlate requests. Examples below.

Suggested next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive w/ engineering (45–60m) — propose Fri Jul 17 10:00 PT — go/no-go for POC.
2) Share internal schema & example logs so we can map fields.
3) Provide short-lived test keys + sandbox access.

Quick auth/observability snippets (high level):
- SDK init (python):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
  # request: client.generate(..., headers={"X-RW-Trace-Id":"<uuid>", "X-RW-Route":"support-prod"})

- Observability headers to propagate: X-RW-Trace-Id, X-RW-Request-Id (optional), X-RW-Route.
- Latency breakdown headers returned from service: X-RW-Latency-Total, X-RW-Latency-Infer, X-RW-Latency-Batching, X-RW-Latency-Network.
- Logging fields we recommend adding to your logs when proxying: request_id, trace_id, model, model_version, route, cached (true/false), tokens_in, tokens_out.

I've attached the architecture diagram you shared during the call for our notes and attached our SDK auth quickstart + observability spec. Looping in Rishi (pricing) and Vivek (solutions) for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Marissa

Great questions — looping in Vivek and Stephanie to cover the technical details. Answers at a glance: 

1) Latency: typical patterns we see — embeddings generation and vector lookup (when using a fast ANN store) is often <50ms for a single embed + search; lightweight rerank (cross-encoder) can be in the ~120–250ms range depending on model and input length. We can recommend a low-latency model family for rerankers and A/B test accuracy vs latency.

2) Trace correlation: use X-RW-Trace-Id (we recommend UUID v4). We echo X-RW-Trace-Id in responses and also surface it in logs. If you already have a trace id (OpenTelemetry trace/span ids), we can accept those too in X-RW-Trace-Id and map them into our tracing pipeline.

3) Auth rotation: yes — short-lived tokens via an exchange endpoint are supported for Private & Dedicated. For Hosted, we provide rotation helpers and API for key creation/rotation; we also support KMS-backed keys. Vivek will provide a short snippet for rotation flows.

4) Tool-calling example: Redwood can emit a structured JSON payload for a tool call; you can secure webhooks with an HMAC signature header (we provide shared secret setup). We'll include example payload + signature validation notes in the deep-dive doc.

Confirming Fri Jul 17 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Vivek — can you prepare an example SDK snippet for embeddings + reranker and an observability sample (headers & sample dashboard KPIs)? Stephanie — please include CS onboarding checklist and sandbox credentials scope.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Alex / team — Vivek from Solutions. Quick technical notes and examples to help your architects prep for Fri's deep-dive.

SDK auth & rotation (high level):
- Hosted: API key header Authorization: Bearer <key>. Use our key-management API to create short-lived keys (TTL configurable). Example flow: service mints short-lived key via server-to-server call using a long-lived admin token.
- Private/Dedicated: OIDC support + service-account tokens; KMS/HSM integration for key material.

Routing & per-request hints:
- Per-request header example: X-RW-Route: support-prod (policy selects model variant / capacity pool)
- Route metadata we populate: route, shard, model_variant (useful for debugging).

Structured output / tool calling example (truncated):
- Request triggers tool call event; Redwood returns: {"tool_call":{"name":"get_account_balance","args":{"account_id":"1234"}},"metadata":{"confidence":0.95}}
- We sign outbound webhook with X-RW-Signature and include X-RW-Trace-Id for correlation.

Embeddings + reranker pattern (recommendation):
- Step 1: embed query -> ANN search (topN candidates)
- Step 2: rerank topK with lightweight cross-encoder model (model choice drives latency vs accuracy)
- Latency guidance (observed): embeddings generation: ~20–60ms (per request, depending on batch), ANN lookup: ~5–30ms, reranker: ~120–250ms (cross-encoder), end-to-end candidate+rerank typical ~150–300ms. For sub-300ms UX target we recommend batching, candidate pruning, and using a compact reranker model.

Observability hooks (recommended):
- Inbound request headers to set: X-RW-Trace-Id (UUID), X-RW-Request-Id (your internal id), X-RW-Route.
- Response headers we populate: X-RW-Trace-Id, X-RW-Request-Id (if provided), X-RW-Latency-Total, X-RW-Latency-Infer, X-RW-Latency-Batching, X-RW-Cache-Hit (true/false).
- Logging fields we recommend you capture when proxying requests into your logs: {request_id, trace_id, route, model, model_version, cached, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_total_ms}.
- Correlation: store trace_id in your logs and expose it as a link in your dashboard back to Redwood request explorer (we can provide a URL template).
- Sampling: if traffic is high, recommend 1% full debug trace sampling + 100% latency metrics and error metrics.

Dashboard KPIs to track in initial POC:
- 95th pct latency (user path)
- Token cost per request (avg)
- Error rate (5xx) by route/model
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV caching)
- Reranker avg latency and 95th pct

Attachments: short sample observability JSON with header examples and a small SDK snippet for embeddings+rerank.

I'll bring a couple of live snippets to Fri's call and a short demo of response headers in our sandbox.

Cheers — Vivek
